baseline: 0.13.51 coordinator worktree; Linux x86_64 / Python 3.14.10 / PyTorch 2.15.0
implementation: Root-model assembly edit add/set/remove remains an explicit application operation: it edits only named top-level injection seams, resolves component IDs to exact locked versions, parses parameters, and verifies saved component references.

Every candidate is constructed and validated before persistence. Dry-run does not write; failures and user cancellation retain the project configuration; successful commit uses versioned project-config history and preserves existing variant snapshots.

Interactive confirmation is now bound to the candidate base_config_revision. If another process changes project.json while the confirmation prompt is open, confirmation returns PROJECT_CONFIG_CONFLICT and leaves the concurrent configuration intact.
The final write still uses update_versioned with the candidate base revision, so a change after the confirmation retry loads its baseline is also rejected by the store CAS lock.
Assembly UI summaries show the exact seam and construction/forward evidence; project config history/selected-field restore provides the existing history-based undo/redo route.

validation.result: passed: 3 PTY scenarios covering non-persisting preview, add/set/remove with failure and cancellation, and concurrent project config change during the confirmation prompt.
passed: operation readiness and input/configuration provenance are shown.
passed: saved assembly seams are used by inspect/probe/try/repeat and existing variants retain their snapshot.

integration_patch: ExecutionContext carries the candidate config revision only during the explicit confirmation retry; direct CLI commands retain their existing explicit-command behavior.
Assembly persistence remains in the configuration service because the public schema is project defaults; variant edits remain handled by the existing transactional edit service.
